title: Severe Bleeding Control
content:
General information only - not a substitute for hands-on first-aid training. Severe bleeding is life-threatening and time-critical. Summon emergency help as early as possible.

The core principle is direct pressure:
1. Protect yourself - use gloves or a barrier if available.
2. Press firmly and directly on the wound with a clean cloth or dressing, using the heel of your hand.
3. Keep pressing. Do not lift to peek - that breaks the clot. If blood soaks through, add more material on top and keep pressing; do not remove the soaked layers.
4. If you can, have the injured person lie down, and keep pressing continuously.

If bleeding from a limb is severe and will not stop with pressure, a tourniquet can be lifesaving. Tourniquet use is a trained skill - apply above the wound (between wound and torso), tighten until bright bleeding stops, and note the time. Once applied, it should be managed by medical professionals; do not loosen it casually.

After bleeding is controlled, keep the person warm and still and monitor for signs of shock until help arrives.

Get proper training (such as a recognized 'Stop the Bleed' or first-aid course) so these steps are practiced, not improvised.
